dublinCore.title: Quantization and Noise Shaping
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
Quantization
Quantization Noise
Oversampling
Noise Shaping
dublinCore.description: Quantize a full-scale sinusoid, triangle wave or three-harmonic waveform with 1 to 16 bits. Time plots show the quantized staircase and the error, and an FFT of the error shows how oversampling and first- or second-order noise shaping change the signal-to-quantization-noise ratio in the signal band.

learningObjectives: Explain why quantization is irreversible and why the error is bounded by half a step
Predict the SQNR of a full-scale sinusoid from the bit depth
Describe the quantization error in time and in frequency, and say when the white-noise model fails
Explain how oversampling and noise shaping raise the SQNR in the signal band without lowering the total noise
Evaluate when noise shaping helps and when it makes the in-band SQNR worse

misconceptions.misconception: Quantization error is always white noise that is unrelated to the signal
misconceptions.correction: For few bits the error is a distortion locked to the signal, so the white-noise model overestimates the SQNR
misconceptions.evidence: At 4 bits and 16x oversampling the banner shows 28.5 dB measured against 37.9 dB for the model

misconceptions.correction: Noise shaping moves the noise above the signal band and increases the total noise power
misconceptions.evidence: At 4 bits and 16x, second-order shaping raises the total noise from -25.3 to -18.1 dBFS while the in-band noise falls

misconceptions.misconception: Oversampling adds resolution without any filtering
misconceptions.correction: The total noise does not depend on the sampling rate; the gain appears only when a low-pass filter discards the noise above the signal band
misconceptions.evidence: The total-noise figure stays at -25.3 dBFS at 4 bits for every oversampling ratio; only the in-band figure improves

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Four plots: a full-scale waveform, its quantized version with the quantization levels drawn, the quantization error, and the spectrum of the error with the signal band shaded. A banner gives the step size and the measured and predicted signal-to-quantization-noise ratio. Five controls set the signal, the oversampling ratio, the bit depth, the noise shaping order and whether the low-pass filtered output is shown.

controls.label: Oversampling
controls.description: Sets the sampling rate to this multiple of 40 kHz

controls.label: Bit depth b
controls.description: Number of bits of the quantizer; the step size is 2 / 2^b

controls.label: Noise shaping
controls.description: Order of the error-feedback loop around the quantizer

controls.label: Show low-pass filtered output
controls.description: Overlays the output of an ideal 20 kHz low-pass filter and the error left after it

visualElements.description: Original full-scale waveform over four milliseconds
Quantized staircase with the quantization levels and, optionally, the low-pass filtered output
Quantization error in units of the step size
Error spectrum in dBFS with the signal band shaded and the white-noise model dashed
Banner with the step size and the measured and modeled SQNR; in-band and total noise under the spectrum

model.description: Quantizes a band-limited full-scale waveform with a mid-rise uniform quantizer, optionally inside a first- or second-order error-feedback loop, and measures the error spectrum with a radix-2 FFT over seven whole cycles of the signal
equations: white-noise model: noise power = delta^2 / 12, spread evenly from 0 to fs/2
SQNR = 6.02 b + 1.76 dB for a full-scale sinusoid
noise transfer function: 1 - z^-1 (1st order), (1 - z^-1)^2 (2nd order)
assumptions: Mid-rise uniform quantizer with levels at the midpoints of the steps
The signal band is 0 to 20 kHz and the sampling rate is OSR times 40 kHz
The measured SQNR uses a 512 x OSR point FFT of the error over 7 whole cycles of the signal
The noise shaper is an error-feedback loop whose quantizer has extra headroom levels beyond full scale
The low-pass filter is ideal (FFT bins above 20 kHz are set to zero)

instructionalStrategies: Predict from the formula, then compare with the value measured from the samples
Contrast the measured SQNR with the white-noise model at few and many bits
extensions: Add a dither option and show how it decorrelates the error from the signal
Add a third-order shaper and compare its stability range
